title: USHMM's figures for the 1915–1916 Armenian killings, and Turkey's 'controversy' framing
summary: The museum calls it a genocide and gives a death range. The Turkish foreign ministry's page title frames 1915 as a historical controversy.
body: The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum's overview says the Armenian Genocide (1915–1916) refers to the physical destruction of Armenian Christian people in the Ottoman Empire. It says about 1.5 million Armenians lived in the empire in 1915, and that at least 664,000 and possibly as many as 1.2 million were killed between spring 1915 and fall 1916, in massacres, individual killings, exposure, and starvation. The Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs publishes a page titled "1915 and the Turkish-Armenian Controversy over History." The word genocide did not appear in the ministry text our fetch extracted, which was mostly navigation, so this card does not invent the ministry's legal argument. It records that the ministry frames the events as a controversy. The killings and the death range are the museum's researched figures. The legal name is disputed by the Turkish state. That dispute does not erase the museum's range, and the range is still a range.
